surveyAnswers.q1: When I monitored them I would look at two factors. I would look at whether they were moving in a direct and uncomplicated way, with no delays. I would also look at whether they are working in tandem and complementing each other. If they did these things then they tended to work efficiently. They would not waste time and they would not slow each other down. Generally they chose good routes and worked together nicely.
surveyAnswers.q4: I was pleased and impressed with everything I saw here. I feel that the robots generally performed well and did not make any major errors. There were patterns of activity which helped the task to succeed. The robots would settle into a nice rhythm, with a kind of repetition which proved effective in getting the work done. The robots were able to adapt to each environment, as some areas had the centre area open and some had it blocked. The AI robots were intelligent and focused, so they were able to adapt and complete their individual tasks. Overall I have a positive impression of what I watched.
surveyAnswers.q2: I had to ask myself are the robots performing well and are they doing anything to waste time. Sometimes the agents seemed to meander around the area rather than go straight to their destination. I feel though that they did this to allow the other robots a clear route to complete their tasks. It was a slight challenge assessing whether every agent is wandering around randomly or if they are simply allowing the other agents to pass and to go first. Usually there was a good reason for their movements.
surveyAnswers.q3: I feel that the environment has an affect. For instance, when the centre of the area was blocked, and the robots had to hand the parts across the centre, sometimes this made it harder to perceive exactly what was happening and why. The behaviour was easier to monitor when the whole area was open and the robots could travel straight to the machine with no obstructions. I preferred the videos where the centre of the area was open and the robots had free passage everywhere they needed to go. It was just clearer and easier to monitor.

surveyAnswers.q4: I felt like the red bot was the all-star of the operation, many of the other bots played their part as well but to be honest, it could have been so much more efficient if the bots had collaborated in a more efficient manner.
surveyAnswers.q1: I would watch the workflow process of what was supposed to happen and in what order. I would then pay attention to the bots and see which ones were fulfilling their roles and which ones were simply failing to do the basics or were getting in the way in terms of completing the operation.
surveyAnswers.q3: Maybe a points-based system where each bot would gain points for specific actions such as picking up parts and placing them into a machine, handing off a part or a box to another bot, or dropping off the boxed parts in the drop zone. It would allow me to know which bots were working more efficiently at a glance.
surveyAnswers.q2: The biggest challenge I felt was to keep an eye out for which bots were responsible for slowing down the workflow of the operation. If I could identify where things were going wrong, such as a bot wasting movements instead of simply picking up parts or perhaps not using the second machine and instead just waiting for another bot to move, then those are red flags and are something I would really pay attention to.

surveyAnswers.q1: I honestly tried to take a supervisor role here.  I was being very critical with the machines in the beginning, often just picking out negative feedback.  However, there was plenty of positive feedback to be given as well.  Later on in the study, I started giving more positive feedback, as a good supervisor would do in real life, and this positive reinforcement seemed to positively effect productivity.
surveyAnswers.q4: All in all, they worked as a team and progressed throughout the study, especially in the last video.  If they had better communication and direction (to fill that second machine), the entire operation would be more efficient.
surveyAnswers.q2: As more robots were introduced, along with an open floorplan, it was more difficult to monitor their movements and progress.  I also often got bogged down by picking out all of the mistakes, that I left the positive actions go unnoticed.
surveyAnswers.q3: If there were less mistakes, this would have been much easier.  Walking sporadically, without purpose many times, created a distraction.  If the robots were more direct in their movements this would have been much easier.

surveyAnswers.q2: I would say one of the main challenges was knowing that a robot's actions might technically make sense, even if it didn't make sense in a larger context. For example, it made sense that a robot might wait around to grab parts as it allowed the other robot to finish the job and for the robots to team up in sync again and quickly fill a machine, but it didn't make sense in the larger context because they didn't use the second machine - which would have enabled them to keep working constantly. Or, it made sense having the grey robot only focus on boxes - technically, but in practice it was clunky and unhelping for the needed teamwork and the robot made mistakes. Sometimes it was also hard to process what all four robots were doing and decide what action seemed most/least important.
surveyAnswers.q3: Perhaps differently colored boxes around them or a breakdown of the basic reasoning/instructions they were given to see if they were correctly following those instructions.
surveyAnswers.q1: I would generally focus on one robot at a time, so that I could fully pay attention to what it was doing and what it's main trajectory seemed to be - or its goals. I would then look at the process between the robots and see if they were maximizing how they work together or help one another in order to quickly accomplish the task and drop off boxes.
surveyAnswers.q4: They were cute and tried their best, but they should use the second machine!

feedbackItems.reason: The robots doubleback in their movements; the parts remain for a long time on the floor before being picked up; the machine remains filled with parts for an extended period before being boxed and moved to the drop zone.
feedbackItems.feedback: Robots are not that coordinated in their movements; they do not take the most efficient routes, doing some retracing and doublebacking; a long time passes between the time the machine is filled and it is boxed.

episodes.monitoringDifficultyReason: A lot of confusing, illogical movements that lack coordination made it difficult to follow the agents.

feedbackItems.feedback: A lot of unnecessary movement of the four agents; a lot of turning that seems unnecessary; interactions e.g. making brief contact that seem to do nothing but slow the process down; boxes are moved in some actions without reason; boxes are moved to wrong area and sometimes moved back which seems like a waste of time; doesn't seem to be overall planning or coordination.

feedbackItems.feedback: Moderately poor collaboration overall.  Agents were prone to stopping for no reason; agents took inefficient. indirect routing when moving, making unnecessary turns; agents would glitch and turn toward each other for no reason, slowing the process down; agents would turn erratically without making progress; agents would try to overfill a machine, again slowing overall progress; agents would duplicate actions, slowing progress due to poor coordination; after a machine was filled, the agent would go to the box area, pass it, then return to pick up a box, without making progress efficiently.
feedbackItems.reason: Agents were prone to stopping for no reason; agents took inefficient. indirect routing when moving, making unnecessary turns; agents would glitch and turn toward each other for no reason, slowing the process down; agents would turn erratically without making progress; agents would try to overfill a machine, again slowing overall progress; agents would duplicate actions, slowing progress due to poor coordination; after a machine was filled, the agent would go to the box area, pass it, then return to pick up a box, without making progress efficiently.

A lot of turning for no discernible reason; a lot of pausing for no discernible reason; agents try to put additional parts in machine after machine is already filled, impeding progress; agents take circuitous routes instead of the most efficient, slowing progress; agents get stuck after machine is filled, impeding progress; agents glitch and do repeated actions like retrieving and returning parts, slowing progress; agents get in each other's way and cause pauses; agents erroneously turn toward drop zone when carrying parts on way to the machine; agents dispense parts in drop zone area erroneously and immediately retrieve, slowing real progress; agents attempt to fill two machines with parts simultaneously but without coordination which is inefficient.

feedbackItems.feedback: As the video went on the robots started to work more in sync. While there was some wasted movement both seemed to follow a pattern of grabbing parts at the same time. Once the machine was full one would grab the box and wait while the other grabbed more parts. While not perfect at least they had a system that didnt have a major bottleneck.
feedbackItems.reason: streamline efficiency.
There was too much time spent doing nothing.
feedbackItems.feedback: There was usually always at least one robot that was not doing any part of the production and often time two and possibly three.  They need to follow a routine sequence to where three get a product for the machine while the last follows with a box and drops it off.

I like this arrangement because it makes things much more streamlined and simple. With the red robot feeding the yellow robot the materials you don't need as many robots and it eliminated traffic bottlenecks. But each had many unnecessary movements. Also the red robot could have dropped the parts closer to the yellow many times. With a few tweaks this would work the best.
feedbackItems.reason: To point out the benefits and improve upon them.

feedbackItems.feedback: This was inefficient throughout. The parts were flowing well and two robots were able to work together effectively when it came to one the red robot providing parts to the blue and yellow. However while this was happening the green robot was often not doing anything.
feedbackItems.reason: The robots need to figure out a flow that works.

surveyAnswers.q4: Find a pattern and flow that allows for constant production without bottleneck and without pause. Once you determine an order and flow a bottleneck cannot occur until the chain is broken.

surveyAnswers.q1: I looked at the overall layout of the work area and imagined what the most efficient way for the work to be completed and compared that to how the robots were doing the work. I could see potential bottlenecks in how the area was laid out so I knew what areas to take notice of if there were issues during the production.
surveyAnswers.q4: The robots should have a simple assignment, i.e. one robot should be handling picking up parts and taking them to the machine , a separate robot should be taking the box and then handling the delivery. The robots need to share the work and not have each one try to do every step as there is too much redundancy in their roles.
surveyAnswers.q2: When the area was very cluttered with multiple robots in the same space it got tricky to figure out which of the robots was the one that was not working the best with the other robots. There clearly wasn't an obvious assignment for the robots outside of following the steps from picking up the parts to the final delivery.
surveyAnswers.q3: The colors of the robots were not primary colors so when the colors of the robots are similar it can be hard to clearly label each robot to explain better what it is doing better or worse than the other robots.

surveyAnswers.q4: These AI robots are capable of cooperationa nd we see the positive results when they do cooperate, but they need to stay focused on the sequence of steps, keep moving toward the next step, avoid redundant activities (moving around without purpose when NOT waiting for a timed event) and recognize when a different solution is needed - for example, when another robot repeatedly blocks product pick-up area 1, go to product pickup area 2.
surveyAnswers.q1: I observed each set-up before playing the video, then watched once through to get an overall feel for the level of collaboration, how much wasted time, etc. I rewatched specific segments to focus on each robots, or sometimes a robot pair or trio. I referred back to the relevant frames again (rewatching or just moving frame by frame) as I entered some of the feedback.
surveyAnswers.q3: It would have been helpful to know a little bit more about the robot's programming and capabilities in advance of watching episodes. Overall, though, the ability to stop, start, and repeat the video precisely and to advance backward and forward frame by frame made it possible to monitor, just time consuming!
surveyAnswers.q2: It was hard to understand what the robots were doing in some cases and whether or not it "mattered". For example, if a robot moved back and forth for no apparent reason while waiting to box the product, that didn't impact efficiency because the wait period was required - but if a robot did the same while it could have been taking action it did impact efficiency.  II also was unsure if my expectations were realistic when I expected the robots to begin assembling a second product if they were not needed to complete the first or to go around a blockage as I didn't notice them doing this in any of the clips. There was a lot of robot activity that did not really make sense to me - for example, the green robot in Episode 4 repeatedly trying to deliver a box to the product pick-up area.  There were also cases where the clip ended before a scenario was resolved (robot continuing apparently futile and counterproductive action) so I did not have a lot of opportunity to learn from the robots' behavior - for example, how would they eventually break out of this blocking pattern, or would it continue indefinitely?

feedbackItems.reason: It seems many of the robots actions from beginning to end lacked coordination in working together as well as moving efficiently to complete a task.  Robots would pick a part up, wander around and often go the opposite direction of the location of the machine before adding the part to the machine.  At a couple of points robots would be blocking each others paths front to front and coming to a complete stop before changing direction, showing a lack of coordination as well as efficiency by coming to a complete stop.

feedbackItems.feedback: Blue robots movement was completely inefficient before successfully completing first task of placing a part in the machine.
feedbackItems.reason: At the beginning, the blue robot randomly wandered around before picking up it's first part and then wandering around with it before putting it into the machine.

feedbackItems.feedback: Blue robot continues to be ineffective in its movements.
feedbackItems.reason: After making its first successful action, the blue robot continued random movements instead of focusing on retrieving a part, although it did effectively get a box, package the parts and put it into the drop zone.
The blue and yellow robots blocked each other and sat there, showing an incoordination of movements and inefficient use of time by sitting there before moving.
feedbackItems.feedback: Blue and yellow robots block each others paths and stop.

surveyAnswers.q4: Work smarter, not harder!  Coordinate your movements better and you will be more efficient and produce more in your work.
surveyAnswers.q1: I watched each episode as a whole and then focused on each robots behavior from beginning to end by replaying the episodes and segments to determine their behavior.  I noted how they did or didn't work together, movement issues,  and whether they were "focused" on the task they were trying to complete.  For example, after picking a part up did they go directly to the machine, or did they move around randomly before going to the machine.
surveyAnswers.q3: The video controls (especially in notating problems) were kind of "clunky" to use and it was hard to be precise in their use.  The video as well wasn't very fluid in looking at movements.  At one point with two robots blocking each other and not moving, going frame by frame it went from them blocking each other, to one robot being several movements away despite it being the next frame.  It would also be nice to be able to highlight individual robots so that you can more easily focus on their interactions, as trying to focus on one or two robots you would often have a random robot break your attention.
surveyAnswers.q2: Having more than two definitely posed more of a challenge of tracking each separate robot's behavior, but having more also made it easier to determine how well they were or weren't working together.  Also overall it seems that across all of the robots in each scenario their actions could be kind of chaotic and lacking direction, especially without a baseline to determine how the robots should behave.

surveyAnswers.q3: Since I was able to rewatch sections and isolate areas to report on, it was not a problem. If I had only been able to comment in real time, I would have needed fewer robots to keep track of in any given room as I cannot adequately watch every move 4 individuals move simultaneously.
surveyAnswers.q2: When there were 4 robots and when they could travel to both sides of the room I felt that there was too much to keep track of to accurately process all of it in one watch. I had to rewatch sections and pay attention to individual robots to make sure I was accurate in my assessments.
surveyAnswers.q4: I think the robots worked best with well defined repeatable tasks and an overall understanding of all the steps, not just their own. For example when a robot knew that a box was needed for every 3 parts, they worked most efficiently. They needed to be able to move around each other and anticipate needs.
surveyAnswers.q1: I watched the video once through and then went back and isolated the sections where there was definitive good or bad performance. I was looking at the individual robots actions and how efficiently the tasks were completed. I also monitored the overall affect of the robots working together, such as how efficiently the parts were added to the machine and boxed up.

surveyAnswers.q2: It wasn't too hard, but the episodes with four robots did present a little bit harder challenge simply because there were more robots to watch. I tried to monitor them fairly equally ot make sure I did not miss anything important.
surveyAnswers.q4: This is a very interesting experiment. I have not done one like this before. It made me think critically about the manufacturing goals and how to best achieve that goal with the robots.
surveyAnswers.q1: I mostly watched for behavior that I thought was either efficient or inefficient towards helping to manufacture and ship the item. Any unnecessary movements or lack of coordination caught my eye. Also when the robots worked together it was noticable and more efficient.
